thence its powers, namely for expelling, may be rendered stronger; and furthermore, the doses of <term>precipitated Mercury</term> <gloss>a medicinal compound of mercury</gloss> may be more easily formed for administering or swallowing, specifically in the form of pills. Here, therefore, this precipitated Mercury is uniquely praised and commended, and indeed it performs very well. The same is achieved by <term>Mercury of life</term> <gloss>antimony oxichloride</gloss> or <term>flowers of butter of antimony</term> <gloss>antimony trioxide</gloss>, concerning which we spoke above, if 4 to 12 grains of it are administered for three full days in an extract of <term>Hellebore</term> <gloss>a plant used as a potent purgative</gloss> and <term>colocynth</term> <gloss>Bitter Apple, a powerful laxative</gloss>; it expels the resolved salt <note>the excess fluids or "salts" causing the swelling</note> quite successfully. Afterward, however, sweating and urination should be provoked with a decoction of <term>sarsaparilla</term>, <term>holy wood</term> <gloss>guaiacum</gloss>, or <term>asarum root</term> <gloss>wild ginger</gloss>, always adding <term>spirit of Tartar</term> <gloss>a distillate of potassium bitartrate</gloss>, or other <term>diaphoretics</term> <gloss>sweat-inducing agents</gloss> and <term>diuretics</term> <gloss>urine-inducing agents</gloss>, about which we spoke above. Especially important is the addition of the <term>arcanum</term> <gloss>secret remedy</gloss> of wormwood or <term>blessed thistle</term>. Here it must be noted, however, that the three-day administration of Mercury of life in adults often tends to cause a <term>prolapsus ani</term> <gloss>prolapse of the rectum</gloss>, which is afterwards rarely or even with great difficulty cured. In treating <term>dropsy</term> <gloss>hydrops or edema</gloss>, it is necessary to apply such purgatives immediately from the beginning of the cure; afterwards, the diuretics and <term>hydrotics</term> <gloss>water-expelling medicines</gloss> should follow. Otherwise, a <term>histeron proteron</term> <gloss>the reverse of the natural order; putting the cart before the horse</gloss> <note>original Greek: "ὕστερον πρότερον"</note> would be practiced here: all the serum or water would be rolled down to the kidneys and ureters, where afterwards, because of the heavy burden, very persistent symptoms often tend to arise. Furthermore, in the preparation of the extract of <term>black Hellebore root</term>, it is safer to use the wine itself instead of spirit of wine <gloss>alcohol</gloss>, with which the root itself should be gently boiled without loud bubbling; and this must be done with fresh wine until all the essential power has been extracted from the roots; afterward, by evaporating or distilling to the thickness of honey, it should be reduced to an extract. This is because spirit of wine, on account of that by which it prevails in sulfur <note>the volatile, oily principle in alchemy</note> rather than in liquid...

<summary>Crollius details the use of mercury and antimony compounds combined with botanical extracts to purge excess fluids in dropsy cases, warning that proper order in treatment is essential to avoid kidney damage.</summary>
<keywords>Mercury, Antimony, Hellebore, Colocynth, Dropsy, Diuretics, Purgatives, Rectal Prolapse, Spirit of Tartar, Extraction methods</keywords>
